nodes.summary: The automaton accepts exactly the words the regular expression matches.
nodes.title: Correctness of Thompson's construction

nodes.summary: For every regular expression $r$, the number of states of Thompson's automaton of $r$ is $n(r)$, the Thompson state count of $r$: $n(0) = 0$, $n(\varepsilon) = 1$, $n(a) = 2$ for a letter $a$, $n(P + Q) = n(P) + n(Q)$, $n(PQ) = n(P) + n(Q)$ and $n(P^*) = n(P) + 1$.
nodes.title: Number of states of Thompson's automaton

nodes.summary: For a letter $a$ of the alphabet $\alpha$, this is the ε-NFA over $\alpha$ with two states, a start state and an accepting state, and a single move, which reads $a$ and goes from the start state to the accepting state; it has no other moves and no ε-moves.
nodes.title: Single-letter automaton

nodes.summary: Given ε-NFAs $M$ with state set $\sigma$ and $N$ with state set $\tau$ over the same alphabet, their concatenation is the ε-NFA on the disjoint union $\sigma \sqcup \tau$ whose moves are the moves of $M$, the moves of $N$, and an ε-move from every accepting state of $M$ to every start state of $N$. Its start states are the start states of $M$ and its accepting states are the accepting states of $N$.
nodes.title: Concatenation of ε-NFAs

nodes.summary: The state count $n(r)$ of a regular expression $r$ is defined by structural recursion: $n(0) = 0$, $n(\varepsilon) = 1$, $n(a) = 2$ for a letter $a$, $n(P + Q) = n(P) + n(Q)$, $n(PQ) = n(P) + n(Q)$ and $n(P^*) = n(P) + 1$.
nodes.title: Thompson state count

nodes.summary: The ε-NFA over the alphabet $\alpha$ with a single state, which is both its start state and its accepting state, and no moves at all (neither letter moves nor ε-moves).
nodes.title: One-state automaton

nodes.summary: Given an ε-NFA $M$ with state set $\sigma$, its star automaton has the states of $M$ together with one new state $q_0$, which is its only start state and its only accepting state. Its moves are the moves of $M$, an ε-move from $q_0$ to every start state of $M$, and an ε-move from every accepting state of $M$ to $q_0$.
nodes.title: Kleene star of an ε-NFA

nodes.summary: The state set $S(r)$ of Thompson's automaton of a regular expression $r$ is defined by structural recursion: $S(0)$ is empty, $S(\varepsilon)$ has one element, $S(a)$ has two elements for a letter $a$, both $S(P + Q)$ and $S(PQ)$ are the disjoint union $S(P) \sqcup S(Q)$, and $S(P^*)$ is $S(P)$ together with one new element.
nodes.title: States of Thompson's automaton

nodes.summary: To each regular expression $r$ over an alphabet $\alpha$ it assigns an ε-NFA over $\alpha$ with state set $S(r)$, the states of Thompson's automaton of $r$, by structural recursion: $0$ goes to the automaton with no states, $\varepsilon$ to the one-state automaton, a letter $a$ to the single-letter automaton of $a$, $P + Q$ to the union of the automata of $P$ and $Q$, $PQ$ to their concatenation, and $P^*$ to the…
nodes.title: Thompson's construction

nodes.summary: Given ε-NFAs $M$ with state set $\sigma$ and $N$ with state set $\tau$ over the same alphabet, their union is the ε-NFA on the disjoint union $\sigma \sqcup \tau$ whose moves are the moves of $M$ and the moves of $N$, whose start states are the start states of $M$ and of $N$, and whose accepting states are the accepting states of $M$ and of $N$.
nodes.title: Union of ε-NFAs

nodes.summary: Over an alphabet $\alpha$, this is the ε-NFA whose set of states is empty; consequently it has no start states, no accepting states and no transitions.
nodes.title: The ε-NFA with no states

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
